sources.entry: Omeka S - Next-generation web publishing platform for institutions interested in connecting digital cultural heritage collections with other resources online. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Omeka S is a web publication system for institutions such as universities, galleries, libraries, archives, and museums to publish curated online exhibits built on a shared pool of items and metadata.
summary.what_it_does: Omeka S lets an institution run a local network of independently curated exhibits that draw from a collaboratively built pool of items, media, and their metadata. The README describes it as a LAMP application (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP) with a database configured through config/database.ini. Installation can be done from a Git clone or a released zip file, followed by a browser-based setup step. Updates are handled through git pull or by replacing files from a new zip, then running migrations in the web interface. The repository includes a gulp task to build a zipped release, with an option to omit Composer dev dependencies. Omeka-specific code lives under application/. The README lists Laminas, Doctrine 2, EasyRdf, PHPUnit, and jQuery as libraries used, among others.
use_cases: publish digital cultural heritage collections online
build online exhibits for a museum or gallery
manage library or archive item metadata
run a university digital collections website
how_to_run: Make sure Node.js and npm are installed
Clone this repository in your Apache web directory: git clone <repository URL>
cd omeka-s && npm install && npx gulp init
Edit config/database.ini with MySQL username, password, database name, and host (create the user and database first)
Make sure the files/ directory is writable by Apache
Open the omeka-s directory in a web browser to complete installation
notable: Built for shared item and metadata pools across multiple independently curated exhibits
Targets cultural heritage institutions such as libraries, archives, and museums
Supports installation from Git or from a released zip file
Includes a gulp task to build a distributable zip, optionally without dev dependencies
Follows the Laminas Coding Style Guide and git-flow with Semantic Versioning
caveats: Requires a LAMP stack with MySQL and Apache; the README refers to the manual for detailed system requirements
Installation involves command-line steps (npm, gulp) and manual database configuration
Updates should be preceded by a full site and database backup, per the README
keywords: share archive items with the public
